subject: Music Production
title: Digging in the Crates
description: A micro-lesson that makes Digging in the Crates usable.

hook.text: Hip-hop producers spent hours in dusty record stores searching for obscure vinyl to sample.

buildup.text: This treasure hunt, called crate digging, required deep musical knowledge across many genres.

discovery.text: Finding a rare funk break or jazz riff that nobody else had sampled gave a producer a unique sound.

twist.text: Some producers deliberately removed labels from records so rivals could not identify their sources.

climax.text: Crate digging made hip-hop producers into scholars of music history across every genre.

punchline.text: Dusty record shops were hip-hop's secret libraries.

quiz.question: Why did some producers remove labels from vinyl records?
options: To prevent rivals from identifying their sample sources
The labels were damaged from use
